title: bactris pectinata subsp. hylophila
intro: Bactris pectinata subsp. hylophila, commonly known as the "Guama" or "Guabina", is a plant species native to the tropical forests of South America. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties and has been found to have various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities. The therapeutic actions of Bactris pectinata subsp. hylophila include wound healing, antiseptic, and antifungal properties, which make it useful for treating skin conditions and infections. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its therapeutic effects.
